_comment: Copy to config.json and edit for your project. 'topics' must be real conference-data topic names - the dataset does not have one for every subject every year ('ai' does not exist as a 2026 topic file; this example uses 'data' instead, the closest real category to AI/ML conferences, verified live 2026-08-26 - see the README for the full topic list). 'watchlist' entries are venues worth tracking directly regardless of what conference-data indexes, each best-effort scanned for open/closed state at its own cfp_url. Nothing here drafts a pitch or submits anything - scan only discovers, classifies, and records; a human drafts and submits behind the gate.

watchlist.name: KubeCon + CloudNativeCon Europe
watchlist.cadence_note: annual, Europe edition (separate CFPs run for the North America and China editions)
watchlist.format_note: the page states its close date without a year (e.g. 'CFP Closes: Sunday, 11 October'), so best-effort scanning often reports detected_state unknown even while the CFP is open - verify the year by hand before trusting cfp_end here

watchlist.name: Berlin Buzzwords
watchlist.cadence_note: annual, Berlin - search, data engineering, distributed systems

watchlist.name: React Summit
watchlist.format_note: GitNation's CFP pages are client-rendered (a React SPA); a plain server-side fetch typically returns no scannable text at all, so detected_state comes back unknown here by design, not by bug - confirm status on the page directly
